claim: Gravin knockout MEFs exhibit prolonged mitosis compared to wildtype MEFs, with mitosis delayed by 11.9 minutes.
source: In contrast, mitosis was delayed by 11.9 min in Gravin KO cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by time-lapse video microscopy data showing mitotic duration measurements in wildtype versus Gravin KO MEFs, presented in Figure 1B.

claim: Baseline mitotic duration in wild-type MEFs expressing GFP-tagged histone 2B is 32.6 minutes.
source: Live-cell imaging of wild-type MEFs expressing GFP-tagged histone 2B (Figure 1—video 1) established a baseline mitotic duration (nuclear envelope breakdown to anaphase) as 32.6 min (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data measuring time from nuclear envelope breakdown to anaphase in wildtype MEFs.

claim: Gravin depletion reduces pT210-Plk1 immunofluorescence at centrosomes to 80.2% of control levels.
source: Gravin depletion reduced immunofluorescence of pT210-Plk1% to 80.2% of control shRNA-expressing cells (Figure 1C,E).
evidence: Supported by structured illumination microscopy and quantification of pT210-Plk1 signal at centrosomes in Gravin-depleted versus control cells.

claim: Gravin depletion reduces pT288-AurA immunofluorescence at centrosomes to 58.5% of control levels.
source: Strikingly, pT288-AurA signal in Gravin-depleted cells dropped to 58.5% of control cell immunofluorescence (Figure 1D,F).
evidence: Supported by structured illumination microscopy and quantification of pT288-AurA signal at centrosomes in Gravin-depleted versus control cells.

claim: Gravin is required for localizing active pools of Plk1 and AurA at mitotic centrosomes.
source: These findings reveal that Gravin is required for localizing active pools of Plk1 and AurA at mitotic centrosomes.
evidence: Inferred from data showing reduced pT210-Plk1 and pT288-AurA signals at centrosomes upon Gravin depletion.

claim: During interphase, Gravin is dispersed throughout the cell.
source: During interphase Gravin is dispersed throughout the cell (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by SIM micrographs showing Gravin localization in interphase U2OS cells.

claim: In mitosis, pT766-Gravin accumulates at centrosomes.
source: In mitosis, however, pT766-Gravin accumulates at centrosomes, a major hub of Plk1 and AurA signaling (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by SIM micrographs showing pT766-Gravin localization in mitotic U2OS cells.

claim: CLP-BI2536 potently inhibits Plk1 with an IC50 of 49 ± 26 nM.
source: In vitro kinase activity measurements demonstrated that CLP-BI2536 potently inhibits Plk1 (IC50 = 49 ± 26 nM; Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by in vitro kinase assay data measuring Plk1 inhibition with increasing concentrations of CLP-BI2536.

claim: Incubation with 250 nM CLP-BI2536 for 4 hours at 37°C results in approximately 50% labeling of SNAP-PACT.
source: Incubation with 250 nM CLP-BI2536 for 4 hr at 37°C was defined as the optimal drug regimen (~50% labeling of SNAP-PACT; Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: Supported by pulse-chase experiments measuring CLP-BI2536's ability to block CLP-rhodamine conjugation to SNAP-PACT.

claim: In mitotic cells expressing LoKI-off, incubation with 250 nM CLP-BI2536 reduced pT210-Plk1 immunofluorescence to 58.1% of DMSO-treated controls.
source: In mitotic cells expressing LoKI-off, incubation with 250 nM CLP-BI2536 reduced pT210-Plk1 immunofluorescence to 58.1% of DMSO-treated controls (Figure 2G,I).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence quantification of pT210-Plk1 signal at centrosomes in LoKI-off cells treated with CLP-BI2536.

claim: In mitotic cells expressing LoKI-on, incubation with 250 nM CLP-BI2536 reduced pT210-Plk1 immunofluorescence to 21.4% of DMSO-treated controls.
source: Strikingly, the pT210-Plk1 signal was reduced to 21.4% in cells expressing LoKI-on (Figure 2H,I).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence quantification of pT210-Plk1 signal at centrosomes in LoKI-on cells treated with CLP-BI2536.

claim: Application of CLP-BI2536 in LoKI-on U2OS cells increased the incidence of abnormal bipolar and monopolar spindles by 24.6% compared to LoKI-off controls (10.3%).
source: Analysis in U2OS cells revealed that application of CLP-BI2536 in LoKI-on cells increased the incidence of abnormal bipolar (green) and monopolar (purple) spindles by 24.6% as compared to LoKI-off controls (10.3%; Figure 3B,C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by spindle classification measurements in U2OS cells treated with CLP-BI2536.

claim: Targeting CLP-BI2536 to centrosomes impairs accumulation of γ-tubulin at this location.
source: These findings indicate that targeting CLP-BI2536 to centrosomes impairs accumulation of γ-tubulin at this location.
evidence: Inferred from data showing drastically reduced γ-tubulin levels at centrosomes in LoKI-on cells exposed to CLP-BI2536 followed by washout.

claim: CLP-MLN8237 potently inhibits AurA with an IC50 less than 9.5 nM.
source: In vitro kinase activity measurements demonstrated that CLP-MLN8237 potently inhibits AurA (IC50 <9.5 nM; Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by in vitro kinase assay data measuring AurA inhibition with increasing concentrations of CLP-MLN8237.

claim: Treatment with 100 nM CLP-MLN8237 for 4 hours at 37°C is sufficient to label approximately 50% of drug binding sites.
source: Cell-based characterization established that treatment with 100 nM CLP-MLN8237 for 4 hr at 37°C was sufficient to label ~50% of drug binding sites (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by pulse-chase experiments measuring CLP-MLN8237's ability to block CLP-rhodamine conjugation to SNAP-PACT.

claim: In mitotic cells expressing LoKI-off, incubation with 100 nM CLP-MLN8237 reduced pT288-AurA immunofluorescence to 27.8% of DMSO-treated controls.
source: In mitotic cells expressing LoKI-off, incubation with 100 nM CLP-MLN8237 reduced pT288-AurA immunofluorescence to 27.8% of DMSO-treated controls (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence quantification of pT288-AurA signal at centrosomes in LoKI-off cells treated with CLP-MLN8237.

claim: In mitotic cells expressing LoKI-on, incubation with 100 nM CLP-MLN8237 reduced pT288-AurA immunofluorescence to 14.2% of DMSO-treated controls.
source: Importantly, the pT288-AurA signal was further reduced to 14.2% in cells expressing LoKI-on (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence quantification of pT288-AurA signal at centrosomes in LoKI-on cells treated with CLP-MLN8237.

claim: Increasing the local concentration of MLN8237 enhances drug action by approximately 2-fold at centrosomes.
source: Thus, increasing the local concentration of MLN8237 enhances drug action by approximately 2-fold at this subcellular location.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of pT288-AurA reduction in LoKI-on versus LoKI-off cells treated with CLP-MLN8237.

claim: Baseline mitotic timing in U2OS cells expressing GFP-tagged histone 2B is 35.1 minutes.
source: Live-cell imaging of U2OS cells expressing GFP-tagged histone 2B (Figure 4G, Figure 4—figure supplement 2D, Figure 4—videos 1 and 2) was used to calculate a baseline for mitotic timing (nuclear envelope breakdown to anaphase) as 35.1 min (Figure 4H).
evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data measuring time from nuclear envelope breakdown to anaphase in U2OS cells.

claim: Simultaneous application of CLP-BI2536 (250 nM) and CLP-MLN8237 (100 nM) to LoKI-off cells delayed mitosis by 19.4 minutes.
source: Mitosis was delayed by 19.4 min when CLP-BI2536 (250 nM) and CLP-MLN8237 (100 nM) were simultaneously applied to LoKI-off cells (Figure 4G,H).
evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data measuring mitotic duration in LoKI-off cells treated with combination of CLP-BI2536 and CLP-MLN8237.

claim: Simultaneous application of CLP-BI2536 (250 nM) and CLP-MLN8237 (100 nM) to LoKI-on cells prolonged mitosis 3-fold with a 59 minute delay.
source: However, the same combination treatment prolonged mitosis 3-fold (59 min delay) when experiments were repeated in LoKI-on cells (Figure 4G,H).
evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data measuring mitotic duration in LoKI-on cells treated with combination of CLP-BI2536 and CLP-MLN8237.

claim: Multipolar spindles, spindle orientation defects, and prolonged mitoses are evident in drug-treated zebrafish embryos expressing LoKI-on.
source: Multipolar spindles, spindle orientation defects, and prolonged mitoses were evident in drug-treated embryos expressing LoKI-on (Figure 5C, Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging of zebrafish embryos microinjected with LoKI-on mRNA and CLP-BI2536.

claim: Drug-treated LoKI-on zebrafish embryos exhibited microtubule abnormalities and a higher incidence of mitotic cells compared to LoKI-off embryos.
source: In contrast, drug-treated LoKI-on embryos exhibited microtubule abnormalities and a higher incidence of mitotic cells (Figure 5E).
evidence: Supported by fixed-cell imaging of whole zebrafish embryos showing microtubule organization and mitotic cell counts.

claim: Centrosomal inhibition of Plk1 correlates with increased mitotic indices in LoKI-on zebrafish embryos.
source: Additional analyses correlated centrosomal inhibition of Plk1 with increased mitotic indices in LoKI-on embryos (Figure 5F).
evidence: Supported by mitotic index measurements in LoKI-expressing zebrafish embryos treated with CLP-BI2536.

claim: In cells expressing Mis12-LoKI-off, incubation with 100 nM CLP-MLN8237 caused a negligible decrease in pS69-Hec1 signal compared to DMSO-treated controls.
source: In cells expressing Mis12-LoKI-off, incubation with 100 nM CLP-MLN8237 caused a negligible decrease in pS69-Hec1 signal as compared to DMSO-treated controls (Figure 6G,I).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence quantification of pS69-Hec1 signal at kinetochores in Mis12-LoKI-off cells treated with CLP-MLN8237.

claim: In Mis12-LoKI-on cells, incubation with 100 nM CLP-MLN8237 reduced pS69-Hec1 signal to 59.8% of DMSO-treated controls.
source: Conversely, in Mis12-LoKI-on cells the pS69-Hec1 signal was reduced to 59.8% (Figure 6H,I).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence quantification of pS69-Hec1 signal at kinetochores in Mis12-LoKI-on cells treated with CLP-MLN8237.

claim: The pS69-Hec1 signal at centrosomes was unaffected by CLP-MLN8237 treatment in Mis12-LoKI cells.
source: Importantly, the pS69-Hec1 signal at centrosomes was unaffected by drug treatments (Figure 6G,H, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence quantification showing no change in pS69-Hec1 signal at centrosomes in drug-treated Mis12-LoKI cells.

claim: When SNAP-PACT LoKI-expressing cells were used to sequester CLP-MLN8237 at centrosomes, no reduction in pS69-Hec1 signal at kinetochores was observed.
source: Finally, when SNAP-PACT LoKI-expressing cells were used to sequester CLP-MLN8237 at centrosomes, we no longer observed a reduction in pS69-Hec1 signal at kinetochores (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence quantification of pS69-Hec1 signal at kinetochores in SNAP-PACT LoKI cells treated with CLP-MLN8237.

claim: S69-Hec1 phosphorylation is a local event that depends on AurA activity at kinetochores.
source: More importantly, these findings uncover that S69-Hec1 phosphorylation is a local event that depends on AurA activity at kinetochores.
evidence: Inferred from data showing that kinetochore-targeted MLN8237 reduces pS69-Hec1 at kinetochores but centrosome-targeted MLN8237 does not.

claim: Plk1 and AurA are important regulators of cell division.
source: Polo-like kinase 1 (Plk1) and Aurora A (AurA) are important regulators of cell division (Barr et al., 2004; Combes et al., 2017; Lens et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature establishing roles of Plk1 and AurA in cell division.

claim: ATP-competitive drugs BI2536 and MLN8237 block Plk1 and AurA activity and are promising anticancer therapies.
source: Accordingly, ATP-competitive drugs that block their activity, such as BI2536 and MLN8237, ascribe functions to these kinases and are promising anticancer therapies (Steegmaier et al., 2007; Tang et al., 2017; Lénárt et al., 2007; Asteriti et al., 2014; Manfredi et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature describing BI2536 and MLN8237 as kinase inhibitors and anticancer agents.

claim: Plk1 and AurA continually change their location and activity throughout mitosis.
source: However, elucidating the individual spatial and temporal actions of Plk1 and AurA remains challenging as these enzymes continually change their location and activity throughout mitosis (Bruinsma et al., 2015; Joukov and De Nicolo, 2018; Lera et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature describing dynamic localization and activity of Plk1 and AurA during mitosis.

claim: The anchoring protein Gravin/AKAP12 forms a macromolecular complex with Plk1 and AurA.
source: The anchoring protein Gravin/AKAP12 participates in this process by forming a macromolecular complex with these enzymes (Hehnly et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature describing Gravin's interaction with Plk1 and AurA.

claim: A-kinase anchoring proteins (AKAPs) are scaffolding proteins that limit the scope of cell signaling events at distinct cellular locations.
source: A-kinase anchoring proteins (AKAPs) are scaffolding proteins that limit the scope of cell signaling events at distinct cellular locations (Scott and Pawson, 2009; Langeberg and Scott, 2015; Esseltine and Scott, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature describing the function of AKAPs as scaffolding proteins.

claim: Anchored protein kinase A action is constrained to within 200–400 angstroms of the AKAP.
source: For example, anchored protein kinase A action is constrained to within 200–400 angstroms of the AKAP (Smith et al., 2013; Smith et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature measuring the spatial range of anchored PKA activity.

claim: Anchoring of Plk1 and AurA occurs on a phosphorylated species of Gravin at Threonine 766.
source: Likewise, anchoring of Plk1 and AurA occurs on a phosphorylated species of Gravin at Threonine 766 (Canton et al., 2012; Hehnly et al., 2015; Colicino et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature describing phosphorylation-dependent anchoring of Plk1 and AurA to Gravin.

claim: Loss or disruption of Gravin scaffold abrogates Plk1 and AurA organization at centrosomes and promotes mitotic delay.
source: Consequently, loss or disruption of this scaffold abrogates Plk1 and AurA organization at centrosomes and promotes mitotic delay (Hehnly et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature describing effects of Gravin loss on Plk1/AurA localization and mitotic timing.

claim: Plk1 phosphorylates pericentriolar substrates that coordinate γ-tubulin accumulation at mitotic centrosomes to facilitate microtubule nucleation.
source: Plk1 phosphorylates pericentriolar substrates that coordinate γ-tubulin accumulation at mitotic centrosomes to facilitate microtubule nucleation (Lane and Nigg, 1996; Haren et al., 2009; Xu and Dai, 2011) (Figure 3F).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature describing Plk1's role in γ-tubulin recruitment and microtubule nucleation.

claim: γ-tubulin is a protein that interacts with α/β-tubulin polymers.
source: Spindle assembly relies on γ-tubulin, a protein that interacts with α/β-tubulin polymers (Moritz et al., 1995; Zheng et al., 1995).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature describing γ-tubulin's interaction with tubulin polymers.

claim: At kinetochores, AurA phosphorylates serine 69 in Hec1, a subunit of the NDC80 complex.
source: At this location AurA phosphorylates serine 69 in Hec1, a subunit of the NDC80 complex (DeLuca et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature describing AurA-mediated phosphorylation of Hec1 at S69.

claim: Local phosphorylation of S69-Hec1 stabilizes microtubule-kinetochore interaction to safeguard chromosome segregation.
source: This local phosphorylation stabilizes microtubule-kinetochore interaction to safeguard chromosome segregation (DeLuca et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature describing the functional consequence of S69-Hec1 phosphorylation.

claim: Gravin depletion via shRNA-mediated knockdown perturbs mitotic progression.
source: Gravin depletion via shRNA-mediated knockdown perturbs mitotic progression (Hehnly et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature describing effects of Gravin knockdown on mitosis.

claim: Abrogation of Plk1 activity has been linked to mitotic spindle defects that include abnormal bipolar and monopolar structures.
source: Abrogation of Plk1 activity has been linked to mitotic spindle defects that include abnormal bipolar and monopolar structures (Sunkel and Glover, 1988; Lane and Nigg, 1996; Sumara et al., 2004) (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature describing spindle defects resulting from Plk1 inhibition.

claim: Centrosome-localized pools of Gravin-anchored Plk1 and AurA coordinate mitotic signaling events.
source: Yet, an outstanding question that remains is exactly how do centrosome-localized pools of Gravin-anchored Plk1 and AurA coordinate mitotic signaling events.
evidence: Implied as a research question that the study aims to address through development and application of the LoKI system.

claim: Local inhibition of Plk1 and AurA kinases at centrosomes and kinetochores disrupts substrate phosphorylation, spindle organization, and mitotic duration.
source: Finally, we demonstrate that local inhibition of Plk1 and AurA kinases at centrosomes and kinetochores disrupts substrate phosphorylation, spindle organization, and mitotic duration.
evidence: Supported by multiple experimental results showing effects of localized kinase inhibition on various mitotic parameters.

claim: Activities of individual kinases at precisely defined microenvironments contribute to the global signaling events that underlie mitosis.
source: Together, these studies decipher how activities of individual kinases at precisely defined microenvironments contribute to the global signaling events that underlie mitosis.
evidence: Inferred from the collective findings of the study demonstrating location-specific kinase functions.

claim: Gravin constrains enzymes in a signaling island to provide spatiotemporal control of kinase activity.
source: Thus, we suggest that Gravin constrains enzymes in a signaling island to provide spatiotemporal control of kinase activity.
evidence: Inferred from data showing Gravin's requirement for localizing active Plk1 and AurA at centrosomes.

claim: Depletion of Gravin alters Gravin-Plk1 and Gravin-AurA protein-protein interactions which underlie healthy cellular function.
source: Conversely, depletion of this anchoring protein alters Gravin-Plk1 and Gravin-AurA protein-protein interactions which underlie healthy cellular function.
evidence: Inferred from data showing effects of Gravin depletion on kinase localization and mitotic timing.

claim: Organellar targeting of drugs offers a new means to advance the investigation of broad-spectrum kinases at precise locations.
source: Thus organellar targeting of drugs offers a new means to advance the investigation of broad-spectrum kinases at precise locations.
evidence: Inferred from the successful application of the LoKI system to probe local kinase functions.

claim: Using the LoKI system, we are able to definitively establish that Plk1 activity at mitotic centrosomes is a driver in γ-tubulin accumulation and correct organization of bipolar mitotic spindles.
source: Thus, by using the LoKI system we are able to definitively establish that Plk1 activity at mitotic centrosomes is a driver in these processes.
evidence: Inferred from data showing that centrosomal inhibition of Plk1 prevents γ-tubulin accumulation and correct spindle organization.

claim: Embryos treated with centrosome-targeted Plk1 inhibitors have more microtubule abnormalities than those treated with a non-localized inhibitor.
source: We provide evidence that embryos treated with centrosome-targeted Plk1 inhibitors have more microtubule abnormalities than those treated with a non-localized inhibitor (Figure 5C–E).
evidence: Supported by imaging data from zebrafish embryos comparing LoKI-on versus LoKI-off drug treatment effects.

claim: Centrosome-localized pools of Plk1 coordinate mitotic events such as spindle organization and mitotic progression during early zebrafish development.
source: These data implicate centrosome-localized pools of Plk1 in coordinating mitotic events such as spindle organization and mitotic progression during early zebrafish development.
evidence: Inferred from zebrafish embryo data showing effects of centrosome-targeted Plk1 inhibition on mitotic parameters.

claim: Even during prometaphase, when kinetochores may encounter centrosome-associated AurA, S69-Hec1 phosphorylation is solely a kinetochore-associated event.
source: Our data suggest that even during prometaphase, when kinetochores may encounter centrosome-associated AurA, this phosphorylation is solely a kinetochore-associated event.
evidence: Inferred from data showing that kinetochore-targeted MLN8237 reduces pS69-Hec1 while centrosome-targeted MLN8237 does not.

claim: Centrosome-associated AurA is not likely responsible for S69-Hec1 phosphorylation.
source: Thus, we show that centrosome-associated AurA is not likely responsible for this phosphorylation event as has been previously suggested (Chmátal et al., 2015; Ye et al., 2015).
evidence: Inferred from data showing no reduction in pS69-Hec1 at kinetochores when AurA is inhibited at centrosomes.

claim: Isolated pockets of AurA may act independently and concurrently to orchestrate complex cellular events.
source: This allows us to postulate that isolated pockets of AurA may act independently and concurrently to orchestrate complex cellular events.
evidence: Speculative inference based on findings showing distinct effects of AurA inhibition at different subcellular locations.

claim: LoKI platforms can be adapted to acutely probe local signaling in other genetically tractable organisms.
source: We foresee that LoKI platforms will be adapted to acutely probe local signaling in other genetically tractable organisms.
evidence: Speculative statement about future applications based on successful use in zebrafish embryos.

claim: Conjugation of chloropyrimidine (CLP) to other ATP analogs offers a general method to synthesize localizable inhibitors for additional members of the kinome.
source: Second, while derivatized Plk1 and AurA drugs delineate roles for each mitotic kinase, conjugation of chloropyrimidine (CLP) to other ATP analogs offers a general method to synthesize localizable inhibitors for additional members of the kinome (Gower et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature and demonstration of CLP conjugation to multiple inhibitors in this study.

claim: The reduced cell permeability of certain CLP-drug conjugates may necessitate their use at approximately 10-fold higher concentrations than the unmodified drugs.
source: However, it is worth noting that the reduced cell permeability of certain CLP-drug conjugates, including CLP-BI2536, may necessitate their use at approximately 10-fold higher concentrations than the unmodified drugs (Figure 2I versus Figure 2—figure supplement 3B, Figure 4E versus Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by comparison of effective concentrations between CLP-conjugated and unconjugated drugs.

claim: Plasma membrane and mitochondrial targeting domains from AKAP79 and dAKAP1 expand the repertoire of subcellular compartments reached by LoKI platforms.
source: Third, plasma membrane and mitochondrial targeting domains from AKAP79 and dAKAP1 expand the repertoire of subcellular compartments reached by LoKI platforms (Figure 6J).
evidence: Supported by demonstration of SNAP targeting to plasma membrane and mitochondria using AKAP79 and dAKAP1 domains.

claim: Reduced cell permeability of certain CLP-drug conjugates may account for the requirement of long incubation periods and application of higher concentrations of drug.
source: We postulate that reduced cell permeability of certain CLP-drug conjugates may account for both of the aforementioned findings.
evidence: Speculative explanation for observed requirement of 4-hour incubation and high drug concentrations.

claim: It is possible that kinase inhibitor drugs directed to centrosomes have off-target effects at nearby structures such as spindle microtubules.
source: Finally, it is possible that kinase inhibitor drugs directed to centrosomes have off-target effects at nearby structures such as spindle microtubules.
evidence: Acknowledged as a potential limitation of the current approach.

claim: Future advancements of the LoKI platform could include photo-caged inhibitors that are inert until they are ready to be released at the site of desired inhibition.
source: We envision that future advancements of this platform would include photo-caged inhibitors that are inert until they are ready to be released at the site of desired inhibition (Ellis-Davies, 2007).
evidence: Speculative proposal for future improvements supported by citation to photo-caging technology.

claim: Employing photo-caged inhibitors would more strictly define the range of inhibitor action, provide another level of control to the LoKI system, and allow better delineation of the effects of global versus local inhibition.
source: Employing this strategy would more strictly define the range of inhibitor action, provide another level of control to the LoKI system, and allow us to better delineate the effects of global versus local inhibition.
evidence: Speculative statement about anticipated benefits of incorporating photo-caging technology.

claim: Future work could advance the LoKI strategy by providing a system that utilizes multiple self-labeling enzymes to deliver distinct inhibitors to the same location.
source: Although in our study this allowed combined inhibition of Plk1 and AurA at centrosomes, we hope that future work will advance on our strategy and provide a system that utilizes multiple self-labeling enzymes to deliver distinct inhibitors to the same location.
evidence: Speculative proposal for future improvements to enable simultaneous delivery of multiple distinct inhibitors.

claim: Employing orthogonal tagging systems such as CLIP-tag or Halo-tag in tandem with SNAP-tag could eliminate the possibility that CLP-BI2536 and CLP-MLN8237 compete for conjugation to the same targeting moiety.
source: Employing orthogonal tagging systems such as CLIP-tag or Halo-tag in tandem with SNAP-tag could eliminate the possibility that CLP-BI2536 and CLP-MLN8237 compete for conjugation to the same targeting moiety.
evidence: Speculative proposal for addressing potential competition between different CLP-conjugated drugs.

claim: By exploiting knowledge of how AKAPs compartmentalize signaling enzymes, tools have been developed that define the local kinase terrain at the angstrom level.
source: Nonetheless, by exploiting our knowledge of how AKAPs compartmentalize signaling enzymes we have developed tools that define the local kinase terrain at the angstrom level.
evidence: Summary statement integrating AKAP biology knowledge with the LoKI technology development.

claim: The LoKI system allows investigators to probe local signaling events at a level of precision that has not been possible before.
source: This will allow investigators to probe local signaling events at a level of precision that has not been possible before.
evidence: Concluding statement about the significance and novelty of the LoKI approach.
